related_questions.question: How to get over COVID quickly?

text_blocks.snippet: To recover from COVID-19 quickly, focus on rest, symptom management, and potential antiviral treatments. Rest is crucial for the body to heal, and over-the-counter medications can help manage fever and aches. If you're at higher risk of severe illness, consider consulting with a doctor about antiviral medications that can help stop the virus from multiplying, according to the CDC.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on rest, symptom management, and potential antiviral treatments

list.snippet: Prioritize sleep: Aim for more than the recommended 7-9 hours of sleep for adults.
Stay hydrated: Drink plenty of fluids to help your body function optimally and prevent dehydration.

list.title: Over-the-counter medications:
list.snippet: Use acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) to reduce fever and body aches.

list.title: Monitor symptoms:
list.snippet: Keep a close watch on your symptoms and seek medical advice if they worsen or if you develop new symptoms.

list.title: Consult your doctor:
list.snippet: If you are at higher risk of severe COVID-19, ask your doctor about antiviral medications like Paxlovid.

list.title: Antivirals work best early:
list.snippet: These medications are most effective when started soon after symptom onset, according to the CDC.
Isolate: Stay home and away from others to prevent infecting those around you.
Wear a mask: If you need to be around others, wear a high-quality mask (like an N95 or KN95).
Practice good hygiene: Wash your hands frequently, avoid sharing items like utensils and towels, and disinfect surfaces.

list.title: Contact your doctor:
list.snippet: For any concerns or if your symptoms worsen, contact your doctor immediately.

list.title: Emergency situations:
list.snippet: Seek emergency care if you experience severe symptoms like difficulty breathing, persistent chest pain, confusion, or bluish lips or face.

text_blocks.snippet: If you have mild COVID-19 symptoms, you can manage them at home with over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen. For more severe cases, or if you are at higher risk of complications, consult a doctor to discuss potential antiviral treatments.

list.title: Mild Symptoms:
list.snippet: If you have a mild case of COVID-19, you can focus on managing your symptoms. Over-the-counter pain relievers like acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) can help with fever, aches, and pains.

list.title: Severe Symptoms or High-Risk Individuals:
list.snippet: If you have severe symptoms (like difficulty breathing, persistent chest pain, or confusion), or if you are at higher risk of complications (due to age, underlying health conditions, or other factors), it's crucial to seek medical advice promptly. A doctor can assess your condition and determine if you are eligible for specific antiviral treatments like oral antiviral medications.

list.title: Antiviral Treatments:
list.snippet: Antiviral medications like Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir) and remdesivir are authorized for treating COVID-19, but they are typically prescribed for those at higher risk of severe illness. They can help reduce the severity and duration of the illness, but they are not a substitute for vaccination and other preventive measures.

list.title: Consult a Doctor:
list.snippet: It's always best to consult with a healthcare professional to determine the best course of action for your specific situation, according to the Wisconsin Department of Health Services. They can provide personalized recommendations based on your symptoms, risk factors, and other relevant information.
